info.title: The Science Infrastructures API
info.summary: The data library's products, the sensors' observations, the domains' algorithms and the servers' plug-ins, for programs in any language.
info.description: Every endpoint is under /api/v1. Answers are JSON unless stated; errors are {"error": "..."} with the status that says why. Units are SI unless a product states its own; angles in degrees at this boundary; times UTC. See api/README.md.

get.summary: Values at places and an instant
get.description: Bilinear in space and linear in time, exactly as the Earth Atlas's page samples (foundations/physis/js/grid.js): the weights of the grid points with a value are renormalised when they carry at least half the total; else, and outside the grid, the value is null. Directions (a standard name with `direction`, or units `degree`) are interpolated through their unit vectors. Accuracy: half the variable's quantum, plus the error of linear interpolation.

parameters.description: The field's name.

parameters.description: The variable's name, as the field's description lists it.

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Longitudes in degrees east, comma-separated (one, or as many as `lat`).

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitudes in degrees north, comma-separated.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: An instant, UTC: ISO 8601 (an instant without an offset is UTC), `now`, or `now+6h` / `now-1d` (s, m, h, d). Default: now. The value is interpolated linearly between the two stored times around it, clamped to the product's span; a variable whose cell method is a mean, sum, maximum or minimum over time takes the nearest time, and a climatology the instant's month.

get.summary: The grid at a time, or a box of it
get.description: At a stored time when `time` is an integer index (negative counts from the end), or at an instant, between the two stored times around it. JSON answers at most 2 000 000 cells; `format=f32` answers the values as little-endian float32, row-major, rows north to south, NaN for no value, with the grid in the header `X-Grid` (JSON).

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: A box `west,south,east,north` in degrees; west greater than east crosses the antimeridian (on a grid that goes round the Earth).

parameters.name: stride

parameters.name: format

get.description: A source of the sensors' store (observation/sensors/store.py) answers its readings; an observations product (schema observations/1: METAR, NDBC, sensor-<source>) answers as it is written, its rows filtered.

200.description: The readings or the set (GeoJSON for a set, when asked)

post.description: Appends readings to a sensor source, defining it first when `define` is given. Each reading is checked by the store (variables, gross-error limits, place, time); the refused are listed with their reasons. Writes follow the service's policy: refused when read-only; with a token, only with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; without one, refused to a page of another origin.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The source's name: lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens.

get.summary: A source's new readings as they arrive (Server-Sent Events)
get.description: `text/event-stream`: each event is `event: readings`, an `id`, and `data` as JSON {source, readings}; a comment line is a heartbeat, every 15 s. A client that reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` receives the events it missed, of the last 1000.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The sensor source.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The id of the last event received.

post.summary: A pure exported function, called with JSON arguments
post.description: Runs in a persistent Node worker over the unit's public interface (js/index.js); nothing is evaluated. `{"$typed": "Float64Array", "values": [...]}` makes a typed array. Results come as JSON: typed arrays as lists, NaN and infinities as null. A call has a time limit (10 s by default), after which its worker is replaced (504). The units are pure, so a call changes nothing: it is open to every caller.

post.summary: A run of a plug-in; returns its job
post.description: One run at a time, in a process of its own, stopped at a time limit (600 s by default). A run computes and writes only its own products (data/cache/plugins/<id>/), which then appear among the fields; it is open to every caller. `chosen` names the source of each need ({need: "product|level"}); needs not named take the described default.

ObservationSet.description: An observations product (schema observations/1), as data/products/observation_set.py writes it.

EventSet.description: Schema events/1 (data/products/event_catalog.py, disaster_catalog.py, mechanism_catalog.py): rows in the order of `fields`, times in ms UTC.

TrackSet.description: Schema tracks/1 (data/products/disaster_catalog.py): tracks with points [time_ms, lon, lat, observed].

RegionSet.description: Schema regions/1: regions rasterised on a grid (the raster itself is not served; see /regions/{name}/at).

Verification.description: Schema verification/1: scores of forecasts against analyses and observations.

items.description: A field ({kind: field, url, field, api, show}), a sketch, a table or a note.

Error.description: An error: 400 a bad request, 401 a missing token, 403 a refused write, 404 nothing there, 405 a method the path does not answer, 409 a run already running, 411/413 a body without length or too large, 422 a function that failed, 501 not written yet, 503 what this computer cannot do, 504 a call past its limit.

bearer.description: The service's token, for writes when it has one.
